problems.reason: Both sentences state that Kentrosaurus lived in the Tendaguru Formation in present‑day Tanzania.
Both sentences describe the temporal and geographic context of Kentrosaurus as Late Jurassic in the Tendaguru Formation.
Sentences 13 and 14 state the same fact about German expeditions in East Africa between 1909 and 1912.
Sentences 11 and 27 both claim that Edwin Hennig described Kentrosaurus in 1915.
Sentence 28 refers to fossils named in 1914 and classified in 1993 without explaining the change or context of the reclassification.
Both sentences describe the same German expeditions in East Africa yielding hundreds of skeletal remains.
